newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: BOXING-AFRICAN CHAMPION N'GOU LOOKS TO THE BIG ARENA.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-AFRICAN CHAMPION N'GOU LOOKS TO THE BIG ARENA.

text.p: Augustin N'Gou, Africa's new heavyweight champion, is not short of either confidence or undue modesty.
"I am the greatest, I am the strongest," says the 22-year-old Ivorian "I am on my way, I will be ranked among the best in the world."
N'Gou, who stands two metres tall and weighs in at 108 kg, is unbeaten after 17 fights, winning 16 of them by knockout.
He is now convinced he can take on any fighter in the world, including the new World Boxing Association champion Evander Holyfield or Mike Tyson, the man Holyfield sensationally upset on Saturday.
"I can beat Tyson," says N'Gou. "Anyone with blood in their veins, I can beat them."
Manager Yves Binovksy is more cautious.
"If tomorrow we put him in the ring against Tyson, I don't think he will be up to it. We have more work to do and I think that in a year we will be ready."
N'Gou, 23, won the African title at the age of last May 31, knocking out Ghanaian veteran Adama Mensah in the first round.
Mensah, who had held the title back in 1981, succumbed after barely two minutes of their fight here. Officially he was 38 but some reports suggested his true age was closer to 40.
The title had become vacant in July, 1994, after the death of then holder, Zimbabwean Proud Kilimanjaro. Kilimanjaro has been suffering from the AIDS virus.
After starting to box in his early teens, N'Gou turned professional in 1992, won the national title but found little competition in a country with few heavyweight rivals.

"Of course when you love a job you want to take it as far as you can," he said in an interview. "For my part, therefore, I intend one day perhaps to become world champion just as today I have become champion of Africa."
Last month N'Gou knocked out 27-year-old French champion Philippe Houyvet in the first round. In a previous fight, Houyvet had become the only fighter to go the distance with the Ivorian.
Another French boxer, World Boxing Council light-heavyweight champion Fabrice Tiozzo, thinks N'Gau could make it in the international arena.
"He has just become champion of Africa," says Tiozzo. "One thing is clear, the Americans will be afraid of an African who arrives like that, unknown, who is two metres tall and weighs 108 kg.
"Even the big Americans could be afraid of him. Given the choice, they won't fight him."
